reviews.title: TOO MANY UPDATES
reviews.text:
I am having an increasingly negative experience with the YouTube iOS app. It receives weekly updates for no apparent reason, and I only notice them because the app suddenly starts glitching and breaking until I manually go to the App Store and update it.

The lack of coherence is staggering. I don’t have these constant instability issues with any other major app. Currently, the search function for the watch history is completely broken, even on the latest version. Please stop using your end-users as forced beta testers just to meet internal release quotas. Focus on a stable UI instead of thoughtless weekly deployments.

reviews.title: New UI is awful
reviews.text:
YouTube completely changed both its UI and touch controls in an update recently. I hate the changes and would like to see them reverted. It seems like the changes were rushed and untested because of the amount of clunky interactions. 

When swiping to close a video you are required to then hit an x on the video to close it. After the video is finished with its shrinking animation and the x appears the location of the video is adjusted as a new menu raises onto the screen from the bottom. This never used to happen and leads to me attempting to close a video only to reopen the video. 

The menu mentioned above looks to minimalist and all of its character was removed in the redesign. I hate the new version. 

The touch controls were heavily reworked leading to the app doing things it has never done before in response to things I have been doing for years. 

As far as I can tell the calibration for what a tap is and what a swipe is are unoptimized leading to me accidentally opening videos constantly then struggling to close them because of the above mentioned changes. 

Long press functionality has been implemented needlessly and will open a menu repeatedly while I am scrolling. This wouldn’t bother me much if it wasn’t for the menu already having a dedicated button in the first place and interrupting the flow of the app. 

These changes were rushed and poorly tested and something needs to be done to make them not disrupt user experience.

reviews.text:
I’m disappointed with the new YouTube iOS redesign. The previous layout was much easier and more comfortable to use.

Some changes I find frustrating include:

* The Subscriptions section being moved from the bottom navigation to the top.
* The new bottom navigation bar.
* Abbreviated view counts instead of exact numbers in expanded video descriptions.
* The missing Video Details section, including upload dates, likes and views.
* Problems with searching my watch history.

Please consider restoring the previous iOS layout or giving users the option to switch between the classic and new designs.

I hope YouTube listens to user feedback and makes the app more familiar, convenient and user-friendly again. Thank you.

reviews.title: Horrible algorithm
reviews.text: It has been over a year and the app still removes features to make it harder to actually use it how you want. You only get the same 5 topics over and over, and many of them are showing you the same videos you’ve already scrolled past on loop. There’s no point in subscribing to channels anymore, if you watch one video from a channel it will fill your feed with their videos regardless. There’s no function to hide or block channels, so if a creator morally goes against what you want to see they will still be included in searches and there’s no way to indicate you don’t want to see them. And now they removed the only features that actually let you filter what you see, there’s no “new to me” tab anymore, and there’s no way to filter videos only under subscriptions. If you have a creator you like who also posts a lot of community posts, be prepared to spend three times as much time looking for videos because now you get more spam on your feed. That’s the poor user experience when I actually PAY to remove ads, with ads it must actually be unusable. It’s sad.

reviews.title: Your ‘Don’t Recommend’ Button Is Failing People
reviews.text:
I woke up at around 3am after a nightmare and couldn’t get back to sleep. I opened YouTube hoping to distract myself, calm down and bring myself back to earth. Instead, Shorts pushed me deeper and deeper into an algorithmic loop of distressing content, even while I was actively trying to tell it I did not want to see that kind of material.

I have OCD, and that night the algorithm contributed to one of the worst spikes I have ever experienced. It pushed me into a frightening mental state where I was having suicidal thoughts. That is how serious this became.

The “Don’t recommend” button needs far more weight. If I reject a type of content, showing me essentially the same thing from a different creator defeats the entire purpose. It is like giving someone a slice of cake, having them tell you they hate it, and then offering them another slice from the other side of the same cake. It is still the same cake.

YouTube does not know what the person on the other side of the screen is dealing with. They could be grieving, traumatised, mentally unwell, sleep-deprived, or already hanging by a thread. An algorithm that keeps feeding them upsetting content because it generates views and engagement can make a bad situation dramatically worse.

YouTube presents itself as a safe, welcoming platform, but the experience can feel completely different once Shorts locks onto the wrong theme. Removing meaningful dislike signals while leaving users with a weak “Don’t recommend” control feels deep

reviews.title: Going backwards
reviews.text:
Removing Subscriptions from the bottom bar was a step backward. For years, the videos from channels I chose were one tap away. Now I have to go to Home, then reach for the top of the screen to find "Subs." That's an extra step every time I open the app, and on a large phone the top of the screen is the hardest place to reach one-handed.

Meanwhile, Shorts keeps its permanent spot in the bottom bar, so it's clear what YouTube wants me to watch. The app now pushes recommendations and Shorts over the channels I actually follow.

The result is less intuitive, less friendly on bigger screens, and more annoying to use. Please bring Subscriptions back to the bottom bar, or at least let us choose what goes there.
